span.p:
KV bytes per token = 2 x L x H_kv x d x b
Laguna S 2.1 constants: L = 48, d = 128, b = 2 bytes for bf16
n_q, hidden_size, parameter count, expert count and vocab do not appear.
A 118B-A8.5B MoE and a 300M dense model with the same four numbers
cost exactly the same per token.

span.p:
1 latent per token, shared by all heads
d_c = 512 plus d_r = 64 decoupled rope key = 576 wide
Kimi Linear ranks, dropped into Laguna's 48 layers

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
576 x 48 x 2 B
= 54 KiB per token
21x smaller than MHA, 3.6x smaller than GQA-8

div.style: color: rgb(34, 34, 34) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Shape note: all four priced at n_q = 48 on every layer, so the columns are comparable.
Laguna actually runs 72 query heads on its 36 sliding layers, so a true MHA Laguna
is 1584 KiB per token, 8.25x the shipped GQA-8.
Query heads set G, hence decode speed. They never set KV bytes.

div.style: color: rgb(34, 34, 34) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The window edits a different factor: how many tokens are retained,
not how wide each token's entry is. Laguna keeps 12 full layers plus
36 sliding layers at w = 512, so 128k context costs 6.07 GiB, not 24.0 GiB.
Both axes multiply cleanly; they answer different questions.

div.style: color: rgb(61, 15, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
MEASURED GOTCHA: the HF reference caches the EXPANDED form.
modeling_kimi.py:401 runs kv_b_proj BEFORE modeling_kimi.py:413 calls past_key_values.update,
so the cache holds 32 x 128 nope + 32 x 64 rope for K plus 32 x 128 for V
= 10240 elements = 20 KiB per layer per token.
17.8x larger than the latent and 5x larger than GQA-8's 4 KiB per layer.
The advertised win lives in the serving engine's absorb trick, not in the model class.
